Here is a summary of every change made. --- ## What was changed ### `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/api.zip-check.tsx` Two additions in `handleZipCheck()`: 1. **`defaultBehavior === "allow"` branch** — added `cutoffTime: null` and `daysOfWeek: null` to keep the response shape consistent even when there is no zip record to match a rule against. 2. **Allowed zip branch** — after the blocked-zip early return, the function now fetches all active `DeliveryRule` rows for the shop (ordered `priority ASC`) and walks them in two passes: - Pass 1: explicit zip match — checks whether the zip code appears in the comma-separated `zipCodes` field of each rule. - Pass 2: zone fallback — if no explicit match is found, picks the first rule whose `zone` matches the zip record's zone and whose `zipCodes` field is empty/null. The final JSON response for allowed zips gains two new fields: `cutoffTime` (e.g. `"14:00"` or `null`) and `daysOfWeek` (e.g. `"Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu,Fri"` or `null`). ### `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid` Inside `wireWidget()`, in the `data.allowed` branch (the live storefront section, inside the `{% else %}` block), two conditional rendering blocks were added after the existing ETA and Zone lines: - `data.daysOfWeek` — splits on `,`, trims each day, joins with ` · ` (unicode middle dot), renders as `
Delivers: Mon · Tue · Wed · Thu · Fri
`. - `data.cutoffTime` — parses the 24-hour `"HH:MM"` string and converts to 12-hour AM/PM format, renders as `
Order by 2:00 PM for same-day delivery
`. Both new elements reuse the existing `.zcc-meta` CSS class so they inherit the same `font-size:13px; opacity:0.8` styling without any additional CSS changes. The additional class names (`zcc-days`, `zcc-cutoff`) allow merchant custom CSS to target them independently if needed.
